packages.label: רַחֲמִים פְּשׁוּטִים וּתְפִלַּת הַשֵּׁם
packages.reason: The three nodes in this Torah's bechina subgraph all express the same essential identity: the dimension of simple/plain divine mercy (רחמים פשוטים), which the Zohar identifies with Zeir Anpin. The Rebbe teaches that this mercy is structurally identical to 'God's prayer' — the dynamic by which the simple mercy of Zeir Anpin intercedes upward to arouse the Great Mercy of Atika Stima'ah. רחמים פשוטים is the pivot: it is what we can arouse through prayer, it is called 'rachamin stam d'Zeir Anpin' by the Zohar, and it is what constitutes God's own 'prayer' (God's simple mercy beseeching His own Great Mercy on our behalf). All three nodes share the same essential nature — they are different names and descriptions of the same cosmic dimension of accessible, bounded mercy that serves as the vehicle for infinite redemption.
